sloka_devanagari:
कान्तस्ते पुरुषोत्तमः फणिपति: शय्यासनं वाहनं
वेदात्मा विहगेश्वरः यवनिका मायाजगन्मोहिनी ।
ब्रह्मेशादि सुरवरजः सदयितः त्वद्दासदासीगणः
श्रीरित्येव च नाम ते भगवती ब्रूमः कथं त्वां वयम् ॥
sloka_english_transliteration:
kāntas te puruṣottamaḥ phaṇipatiḥ śayyāsanaṃ vāhanam
vedātmā vihageśvaraḥ yavanikā māyā jaganmohinī |
brahmeśādi suravarajaḥ sadayitaḥ tvaddāsadāsīgaṇaḥ
śrīrityeva ca nāma te bhagavatī brūmaḥ kathaṃ tvāṃ vayam ||
meaning: Oh Śhāḍguṇya‑sampūrṇa Devī! Your beloved is the celebrated Purushottama. Ādiśeṣa is Your couch; Garuḍa, embodiment of the Vedas, is both Your throne and vehicle. The world‑enchanting Māyā is Your curtain. Brahmā, Śiva, the other devas, and their consorts are Your servants. Your very name is Śrī — how can mere mortals praise You adequately?
commentary: In this first sloka, ALavandhAr establishes the equal status of Srī Devi with Her consort, declaring Her as Bhagavatī endowed with all the six auspicious qualities (śakti, bala, aiśvarya, vīrya, jñāna, tejas) that characterize Purushottama. The verse underscores that She is inseparable from Him (anapāyinī), surpassing Him in motherly qualities such as daya (compassion), kṣamā (forgiveness), and vātsalya (parental affection). She acts as Purushakāra, interceding on behalf of sinners to recommend their forgiveness. The mention of Adhiśeṣa as Her couch and Garuḍa with the Vedas as Her seat and vehicle reflects Her supreme vibhūti and integral role in cosmic functions. The world-enchanting Māyā is said to be Her shielding curtain, highlighting Her transcendental prowess. This sloka is central to Sri Vaishnava theology, emphasizing Srī Devi’s equal authority and grace alongside the Lord. It is further supported by various scriptures, including the Purushottama Yoga of Bhagavad Gītā and the devotional hymns of the Āḻwārs, which describe the divine couple’s inseparability and mutual exaltation.

sloka_devanagari:
यस्याः स्ते महिमानमात्मन इव त्वद्वल्लभोऽपि प्रभुः
नालं मापुमियतया निरवधिं नित्य अनुकूलं स्वतः ।
तां त्वां दास इति प्रपन्न इति च स्तोष्याम्यहं निर्भयः
लोकैकेश्वरी लोकनाथे दान्ते दयां ते विदन् ॥
sloka_english_transliteration:
yasyāḥ ste mahimānam ātmana iva tvadvallabho'pi prabhuḥ
nālaṃ māpum iyatayā niravadhiṃ nityānukūlaṃ svataḥ |
tāṃ tvāṃ dāsa iti prapanna iti ca stoṣyāmyahaṃ nirbhayaḥ
lokaikeśvarī lokanāthe dānte dayāṃ te vidan ||
meaning: Oh sole empress of the worlds, beloved of the Lord of all! Your majesty is boundless, eternal, and naturally aligned with your nature. Even your own Lord cannot fully comprehend Your kalyāṇa‑guṇas, just as He cannot measure His own glories.
commentary: This second sloka highlights the infinite and intrinsic majesty of Srī Devi, asserting that even Bhagavān, the Lord Himself, is unable to fully comprehend Her auspicious qualities. ALavandhAr stresses the synergistic and inseparable relationship between the Lord and His consort, emphasizing that She is eternally agreeable and supportive in all His activities. The verse expresses the devotee’s bold confidence to praise Srī Devi without fear, relying on the sacred bond as Her servant and one who has sought refuge. This reflects the Purushakāra doctrine, where submission to Srī Devi brings grace and protection. The commentary also cites the insights of Swamy Desikan and PeriyavAcchAn PiLLai who underscore the immeasurability and transcendental nature of Srī Devi’s kalyāṇa guṇas beyond even the Lord’s grasp.

sloka_devanagari:
ईषत् त्वत्करुणानिरीक्षणसुधासन्धुक्षणात् रक्ष्यते
नष्टं प्राक् तदालाभतः त्रिभुवनं समप्रत्यनन्तोदयम् ।
श्रेयः न ह्यारविन्दलोचनमनः कान्तप्रसादादृते
संसृत्यक्षरवैष्णवाद्वसु नृणां सम्भाव्यते किञ्चित् ॥
sloka_english_transliteration:
īṣat tvat karuṇānirīkṣaṇa sudhā sandhukṣaṇāt rakṣyate
naṣṭaṃ prāk t-adālābhataḥ tribhuvanaṃ samapratyanantodayam |
śreyaḥ na hy aravindalocanamanaḥ kāntaprasādād ṛte
saṃsṛtyakṣaravaiṣṇavādhvasu nṛṇāṃ saṃbhāvyate kiñcit ||
meaning: When deprived of Your merciful glances, the three worlds fall into ruin; but even a brief shower of that nectar revives them to unparalleled prosperity. Without the grace of the consort of the lotus‑eyed Lord, no being can attain wealth, kaivalya, or mokṣa.
commentary: In this verse, Srī Devi’s merciful glances (karuṇā kaṭākṣa) are portrayed as the life-giving nectar that sustains the entire cosmos. Without Her gaze, the three worlds and all beings therein face complete ruin and loss of prosperity. However, just a brief shower of Her compassionate glance restores and elevates the worlds to infinite well-being. This underlines Her indispensable role as the source of all auspiciousness, wealth, liberation (kaivalya), and ultimate spiritual attainment (mokṣa). The commentary elaborates on the alankāras (figures of speech) praising Srī Devi’s glance as the vital life principle (viśva sanjīvanam) necessary for all existence. It explains how the grace of Her gaze alone can realize all puruṣārthas (goals of life) — emphasizing Her supreme and life-sustaining function within the Vaishnava tradition.

sloka_devanagari:
सान्तानन्तमहोविभूति परमं यत् ब्रह्मरूपं हरेः
मूर्तं ब्रह्म ततोऽपि तत्त् प्रियतरं रूपं यदत्यद्भुतम् ।
यन्मन्यन्यान्यवसुसो विहरतो रूपाणि सर्वाणि तानि
आहुः स्वैरानुरूपरूपविभवैरगाढोपगूढानि ते ॥
sloka_english_transliteration:
sāntānanta mahovibhūti paramaṃ yat brahmarūpaṃ hareḥ
mūrtaṃ brahma tato'pi tatt priyataraṃ rūpaṃ yadatyadbhutam |
yan manya nnyāny avasuso viharato rūpāṇi sarvāṇi tāni
āhuḥ svairanurūparūpavibhavair agāḍhopagūḍhāni te ||
meaning: The changeless, infinite, supremely glorious Brahman‑form of Hari is itself wondrous, but dearer to Him is Your own marvelous form. In all His incarnations and divine plays, You are inseparably united with Him, assuming matching forms and glories.
commentary: This concluding sloka extols Srī Devi’s eternal and infinite divine form, which perfectly complements and matches that of Hari (the Supreme Lord) in every aspect. It asserts the doctrine of Eka-śeṣitvam — the inseparability and unity of the Lord and His consort. Srī Devi accompanies the Lord in all His avatāras (incarnations) and līlā (divine plays), assuming forms precisely suited to each manifestation, tightly embracing Him without separation (anapāyinī). The commentary explains that these forms are said to be ‘svairānurūpa’ — naturally conforming to the Lord’s own divine manifestations and glories, hidden in their profound mystery. This highlights Her dual role as both the upāya (means) and upēya (goal) of liberation and devotion, demonstrating Her supreme status and intimate identity with Hari in Sri Vaishnavism.
